description: Who may use what in LMA. The single source of truth for the roles of every AppSync operation, every other surface that accepts a user pool token, and every web UI route. lma-ai-stack/test/test_role_matrix.py holds schema.graphql, the role table in docs/user-based-access-control.md and the surface list to this file; the UI, transcriber and Lambda tests named under effectiveRole hold their copies of the role rule to its vectors; integ-tests/test_role_access.py calls the operations on a deployed stack as each role.

roles.Admin: Member of the Admin Cognito group. Every meeting, the configuration and user management.
roles.User: A user in neither the Admin nor the Participant group. Their own meetings and those shared with them, and every meeting source.
roles.Participant: Member of the Participant Cognito group. Reads the meetings shared with them, read-only and without the owner's own material, asks the meeting assistant about them, and enrolls their own voice; no meeting sources, configuration or other meetings.

effectiveRole.description: A caller's role from their Cognito groups: Admin when the groups include Admin, otherwise Participant when they include Participant, otherwise User. The pre token generation trigger replaces the role groups in each token's cognito:groups claim with this one role, keeps any other group, and adds the role to the ID token as the lma_role claim. Implemented by lma-cognito-stack/source/pre_token_generation/index.py, lma-ai-stack/source/ui/src/components/common/roles.js, lma-websocket-transcriber-stack/source/app/src/utils/roles.ts, mcp_api_key_authorizer, mcp_analytics/index.py and user_management; each one's tests check it against these vectors.

capabilities.title: Participant home page
capabilities.notes: Admins and Users open the meetings list instead.

capabilities.title: A Participant's read-only view of the meetings shared with them: the list, and each meeting's transcript (live while it is in progress), summary, meeting chat, recordings and consent record
capabilities.notes: Only meetings whose sharing list names them. Not the owner's own material: the meeting context, checklist, labels, guidance, whiteboards, the assistant's answers, the sharing list and the participant addresses. Recordings play through links the server signs for the meeting; the identity pool gives a Participant no permissions.

capabilities.title: Meetings list and meeting pages: transcripts, summaries, recordings, key frames, notifications, whiteboards, archives and cost
capabilities.notes: Admin: every meeting. User: their own meetings and those shared with them.

capabilities.title: Editing, sharing, deleting and reopening meetings: speakers, summaries, agendas, preparation, labels, guidance and whiteboards
capabilities.notes: Admin: every meeting. User: the meetings each operation's own rule allows (sharing and deleting: their own).

capabilities.title: Meeting consent records
capabilities.notes: Admin: every meeting. User: the meetings they own or that are shared with them.

capabilities.title: The meeting assistant chat on a meeting's page
capabilities.notes: Admin: every meeting. User: their own meetings and those shared with them. Participant: the meetings shared with them, answered with the tools approved for Participant use and from that meeting only, and not added to its transcript.

capabilities.title: The Meetings Query Tool, the knowledge base, the chat buttons, the meeting page's chat notifications, and reading the installed MCP servers and skills
Meeting sources: Stream Audio/Video, Upload Audio, the browser extension and the Desktop Capture App
Virtual Participant: launch, schedule, view, share, end and rejoin
capabilities.notes: Admin: every Virtual Participant. User: their own and those shared with them.

capabilities.title: AWS credentials the web UI signs its own requests with: recording playback and file links, transcript translation, the deployment settings, and Virtual Participant launch
MCP API keys and the hosted MCP server (API key and OAuth endpoints)
capabilities.notes: Admin: every meeting through MCP. User: their own meetings and those shared with them.

capabilities.title: Enrolling your own voice
capabilities.notes: Each person their own voice only: enrolling it, and deleting it.

capabilities.title: Configuration: settings, profiles and their history, prompt templates, chat buttons, voice assistant, transcription engine and cost prices
Installing and changing MCP servers and skills, and importing or exporting their libraries
Consent given in advance: your own consents, a meeting's consent page, and asking to be added to its participant list
capabilities.notes: Each person their own consents only, kept under the email address the user pool holds for them. Giving consent needs that address on the meeting's participant list; someone not on it is told only that, and may ask to be added, which is shown in LMA to the people who see the meeting's participant list.

capabilities.title: A meeting's participant list: changing it and reading whether each person on it has an LMA account
capabilities.notes: Admin: every meeting. User: their own meetings only, not those shared with them, and at most 1,000 different addresses looked up a day. The list itself is part of the meeting record, read with it; the account answer is none or the account's role, nothing else about it.

capabilities.title: Creating Participant accounts for the people on a meeting's participant list
capabilities.notes: Admin: any meeting. User: their own meetings only, at most 25 accounts a day. Only addresses on the meeting's list without an account, and only ever the Participant role; other roles and role changes stay with User Management.

capabilities.title: User Management: adding and deleting users and choosing their roles

backendOnly.description: Answered only to backend roles signing with SigV4 (@aws_iam alone): the meeting pipeline, the Virtual Participant and the hosted MCP server. Every signed-in role is refused them.

alsoIam.description: Operations a signed-in role may call that also accept backend roles signing with SigV4 (@aws_iam beside the role list): the lma CLI and SDK, the Virtual Participant and other backend functions.

transcriber-websocket.title: WebSocket transcriber (Stream Audio/Video page, browser extension, Desktop Capture App)
transcriber-websocket.control: The transcriber verifies the access token on every request except its health check and answers 403 to a role the matrix does not list.

identity-pool-credentials.title: Cognito identity pool credentials for the web UI
identity-pool-credentials.control: The identity pool chooses the IAM role from the ID token's lma_role claim: Admin and User receive the web UI's authenticated role; Participant receives a role with no permissions; a token without a recognised role receives no credentials.

mcp-api-key-endpoint.title: Hosted MCP server, API key endpoint
mcp-api-key-endpoint.control: The API key authorizer reads the key owner's current groups from the user pool on every request and refuses the key unless the owner's role is listed; the MCP server refuses a request whose authorizer context names an unlisted role.

mcp-oauth-gateway.title: Hosted MCP server, OAuth gateway
mcp-oauth-gateway.control: The MCP server derives the caller's role from the cognito:groups claim the gateway forwards and refuses an unlisted role.

probe.description: How integ-tests/test_role_access.py calls the operations. Every operation is called as each role it refuses, with placeholder arguments, and must be refused by AppSync before its resolver runs. Queries are also called as each role they admit and must not be refused; mutations are not, since they change data. Queries listed under skipAllowed call a model and are called only as the roles they refuse. The resolvers of the queries under placeholderRefusedForNonAdmins refuse a non-Admin for a meeting they cannot see, which a placeholder meeting always is, in the same words as AppSync, so they are called only as Admin among the roles they admit. Subscriptions are held to the matrix by the schema contract test only.
